applicability.execution_path: IDENTICAL, which is why this is proven and not reused: every observation was taken in the same CTP invocation, against the same client-server server process, in the same session sequence as the assertions it supports. TWO CHANNELS, recorded under channel `other` because the schema carries one channel per row. (1) SHOW HEAP OOS after the committed INSERT and again after the restart (show_heap_oos_after_insert.out, show_heap_oos_after_recovery.out beside the reference) certifies the INSERT-side demotion -- one OOS file, four chunk records for four rows -- and the presence of the chains after recovery. (2) The server's own recovery log for this database ($CUBRID/log/server/<db>_*.err, copied into the bundle as case-evidence/server_log/ and excerpted in the reference) certifies that the RECOVERY PATH RAN AND REPLAYED WORK: exactly one new 'Log recovery: REDO Phase is started' line after the restart, with 'Log pages to redo: 2, Log records to redo: 83', and 'Log pages to undo: 0, transactions to undo: 0'. Channel (2) is what the independent review's F1 asked for: without it the values could have survived because the pages were flushed before the kill -9, and the specification says proof of an insert path never certifies a recovery path. Neither channel certifies a vacuum or reclaim path, which is why the post-recovery chunk count is asserted as a range.

finding.summary: CLAIM WITHDRAWN (ticket 34, closing the independent review's F2). Until 2026-09-11 this matrix carried two PASS rows for OOS-REP-07 against cbrd_26659_oos_dur01 (att-T14-0026 release and att-T14-0027 debug, testcase commit adbd8b745), with gap_kind none. The catalogue statement in full reads: 'A value larger than one page's maximum single-chunk payload is stored as a chain of chunk records, inserted tail first, and is read back complete and byte-identical; total_data_length excludes every chunk header.' The case's oracle quoted it with the two emphasised clauses removed, and neither is assertable at the private shell seam: chunk insertion order is not observable, and total_data_length is observable only through Oos_recs_sumlen, which the case deliberately declines to assert while the pinned 16-byte chunk header differs from the accepted 24-byte one (OOS-REP-05 / CBRD-26950). A PASS against a statement quoted with its hard half removed is an overclaim, so the rows are withdrawn rather than scoped: the multi-chunk row the case inserts is mandated by OOS-DUR-01's own 'including multi-chunk values' clause and stays covered there. Nothing is erased from history -- both withdrawn rows were PASS, their attempt records remain, and OOS-DUR-01's rows list them. WHO OWNS THIS REQUIREMENT NOW: the catalogue assigns OOS-REP-07 seam public-sql; ticket 18 (public Representation boundaries) covers the single-to-multi-chunk boundary and inherits the two clauses this case could not assert, of which 'total_data_length excludes every chunk header' is withheld at the pin under OOS-REP-05 and must not be promoted from engine output. Until an executed public case exists this is a Delivery gap; it is not a Specification gap (the statement is clear) and not a Capability gap of the engine (the chain is written and read back correctly).

attribution.note: Nothing to attribute: no requirement failure exists, and no case at the requirement's own seam has run yet.
